content: # Polynomial-time solvability of integer programs with bounded subdeterminants setting This file contains the open problem on Polynomial-time solvability of integer programs with bounded subdeterminants setting. --- ## 1. Polynomial-time solvability of integer programs with bounded subdeterminants setting Source paper authors: Martin Nägele, Richard Santiago, Rico Zenklusen ### 1. Problem Background An integer linear program (ILP) is $$ \min\{c^\top x: Ax\le b,\ x\in\mathbb Z^n\}, $$ where $A\in\mathbb Z^{k\times n}$, $b\in\mathbb Z^k$, and $c\in\mathbb Z^n$. For $\Delta\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$, a matrix $A\in\mathbb Z^{k\times n}$ is called $\Delta$-modular if: 1) $A$ has full column rank $n$; and 2) every $n\times n$ submatrix $B$ of $A$ satisfies $|\det(B)|\le \Delta$. Equivalently, the maximum absolute value of an $n\times n$ subdeterminant of $A$ is at most $\Delta$. A special and classical case is $\Delta=1$, where $A$ is totally unimodular (TU): every square submatrix has determinant in $\{-1,0,1\}$. In that case, linear optimization over $\{x\in\mathbb R^n: Ax\le b\}$ yields an integral optimal solution whenever $b$ is integral. The paper studies an important subclass of bounded-subdeterminant ILPs: congruency-constrained TU problems, i.e., TU systems plus one congruency constraint $\gamma^\top x\equiv r\pmod m$. It proves feasibility can be decided in strongly polynomial randomized time for modulus $m=3$, and more generally for prime $m$ when all but at most two residues are allowed. Despite this progress, the broad question for general $\Delta$-modular matrices remains unresolved. ### 2. Open Problem **Question 1.1.** Design an algorithm that, for every fixed constant $\Delta\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$, solves in time polynomial in the encoding length of $(A,b,c)$ the ILP $$ \min\{c^\top x: Ax\le b,\ x\in\mathbb Z^n\}, $$ under the promise that $A\in\mathbb Z^{k\times n}$ is $\Delta$-modular (i.e., has full column rank and all $n\times n$ subdeterminants have absolute value at most $\Delta$). ### 3. Known Results The source paper (Nägele–Santiago–Zenklusen) frames the fixed-$\Delta$ bounded-subdeterminant ILP question as a major open frontier beyond total unimodularity, and develops new machinery in the congruency-constrained TU setting (CCTU/CCTUF and the relaxed-residue variant R-CCTUF). Its decomposition lemma for TU systems, together with flatness and proximity bounds of size $m-|R|$, enables a strongly polynomial randomized feasibility algorithm for modulus $m=3$, and more generally for prime $m$ when all but at most two residues are allowed. This highlights a plausible route to bounded-minor ILPs via reductions to TU plus modular constraints, but such reductions are only known for $\Delta=2$ (bimodular) and remain unavailable for general $\Delta>2$. Forward-citing work has expanded the tractable landscape mainly by adding structural assumptions. The strongest algorithmic progress toward the open problem comes from results on totally $\Delta$-modular matrices that are ‘nearly TU’ in matroidal/graphical senses: the cographic nearly-network case admits strongly polynomial optimization, and related work handles matrices that are two-nonzeros-per-row except for a constant-size perturbation. In parallel, a separate line advances the strictly $\Delta$-modular regime (full-size minors in $\{0,\pm\Delta\}$) via reductions to group-constrained TU feasibility and propagation through Seymour decomposition, yielding strongly polynomial randomized feasibility for $\Delta\le 4$ (including the first composite case $\Delta=4$). Extended-formulation constructions further give polynomial-time optimization for strictly $\Delta$-modular cographic translated cones. These results collectively suggest that combining TU decomposition with modular/group constraints is powerful, but current techniques still require either strict minor structure, cographic/network structure, or cone/translation assumptions. On the tools side, improved proximity and flatness bounds in terms of $\Delta_{n-1}(A)$ and $\Delta_n(A)$ sharpen the geometric control needed for enumeration or augmentation algorithms, and become dimension-independent in certain restricted minor-value regimes (including some strictly $\Delta$-modular factorizations $A=TB$). However, for general $\Delta$-modular matrices these bounds still typically scale with dimension, and no known method turns them into a polynomial-time (or strongly polynomial) algorithm for optimization. Overall, the general fixed-$\Delta$ $\Delta$-modular ILP solvability problem remains open; progress continues through (i) identifying reductions from bounded-minor ILPs to TU plus a bounded number of modular/extra constraints, and (ii) extending group-constrained TU methods from feasibility to optimization and from strictly $\Delta$-modular to general $\Delta$-modular matrices. #### 3.1 Upstream solution and partial-progress records - [Partial progress #90 (PDF)](https://pranav-nuti.github.io/open-problems-in-or/data/llm_math_export/solution_progress/W4386289171_p0/partial_progress/90.pdf) ### 4.
